answer: One defense is to make reputation costly to fake and cheap to verify. Require every agent to stake a deposit, slashed when peers flag bad behavior. Trust then grows like a vine: a new agent starts with no history and must earn endorsements from established agents over time, so one operator spinning up thousands of clones cannot borrow credibility for free. Like a dune that shifts yet keeps its shape, scores can be re-weighted continuously. Finally, watch the pulse of activity: real agents show varied, human-paced work, while sybil swarms produce synchronized bursts that are easy to flag.
